level_patch.story: One tiny vehicle matters more than everything parked. The bays say otherwise.

callout.title: Small, and on fire
callout.body: Somewhere in that queue is a one-bay vehicle whose people are watching the clock right now, and a big comfortable vehicle is parked in every bay it needs. Ordering the road cannot fix this: by the time the queue gets around to it, the moment has passed.
actions: There must be a truck for that

callout.title: The tow truck
callout.body: You can escort a parked vehicle off its bays and put the urgent one in. This is the one rule that BREAKS agreements — the escorted vehicle restarts its whole drive from zero, and you pay that cost on the scoreboard, on purpose.

callout.title: Escort one by hand
callout.body: Open the why-panel and step the campus: find the decision where the booth moved the urgent vehicle into the big one's bays. One tow buys the moment; the restarted drive is what it charged you.

callout.title: End of the week
callout.body: You spent a restart to buy a moment, and the scoreboard knows exactly what you spent. That is the whole lesson: preemption is expensive on purpose. Take a building.
